_comment: Known sub-44px controls on AUTHENTICATED phone screens, measured by
authed-phone.spec.ts in the `mobile-auth` lane. Same contract and same
ratchet semantics as undersized-target-baseline.json: the spec fails on
anything NOT listed here, so this file can only shrink.
IT IS A SEPARATE FILE ON PURPOSE, AND THE REASON IS A TEST THAT CAUGHT ME.
The public baseline is pinned by target-ratchet.test.ts to cover EXACTLY the
routes the smoke spec visits — no more, no less — because a route present in
one and absent from the other either turns every known control into a
regression or hides them all. Adding /core/trades to that file broke the
assertion immediately, which is the invariant working. Relaxing it to a union
of two specs' routes would have weakened a check that does real work in order
to accommodate a new lane; a second file keeps it exact.
The two lanes also have different lifecycles. `mobile-smoke` gates every PR;
`mobile-auth` is new, is not a required context, and is expected to churn
while authenticated screens get measured for the first time. Mixing their
debt into one file would make neither readable.
/core/trades STARTS EMPTY because nothing has ever rendered it at 390px.
`/core/*` redirects to /login without a session and to /import without a
league, so every mobile check this repo had stopped at the marketing routes.
A red first run is debt being surfaced for the first time, not a regression
anyone introduced — baseline what it finds deliberately, one entry at a time,
and only where the control is genuinely pre-existing debt being deferred.
⚠ Trade Center's four primary actions were sized by CSS specificity, not by
this file: `.af-tc-actions .af-btn` was (0,2,0), dead equal to
`.af-core .af-btn { min-height: 36px }`, so 44px applied on a coin toss
decided by stylesheet order. Fixed by prefixing with `.af-core`. If entries
appear here for `.af-btn` controls, check the specificity before baselining —
a losing rule looks exactly like a missing one.
